question: What is the main goal of doing a patient interview in nursing?

options.A: To enforce hospital rules on reluctant patients
options.B: To diagnose complex surgical conditions independently
options.C: To gather subjective health data from the patient
options.D: To prescribe appropriate medications for the illness

explanation: You've got this! An interview is simply a friendly, goal-driven chat to find out how the patient feels in their own words (that's subjective data!). [learn more](GNS112_U3_T3#GNS112_U3_T3_h1)

question: How is nursing counselling different from a standard patient interview?

options.A: Interviewing is exclusively used for surgical patients
options.B: Counselling focuses on coping and emotional support
options.C: Counselling is only performed by licensed psychiatrists
options.D: Interviewing requires a formal psychological degree

explanation: Think of it this way: interviewing is about collecting facts, while counselling is about giving a listening ear and emotional support to help patients handle health challenges. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T3#GNS112_U3_T3_h1)

question: To use the 'therapeutic use of self' effectively, what does a nurse mainly need?

options.A: Hiding all personal emotions from the patient
options.B: Strict adherence to strict hospital administrative rules
options.C: Focusing solely on the patient's physical vital signs

explanation: Spot on! Using yourself therapeutically means being aware of your own actions and words so you can connect with and help your patient better. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T3#GNS112_U3_T3_h2)

question: Why is clarification such an important communication skill when talking with patients?

options.A: It proves to the patient that the nurse is in charge
options.B: It speeds up the formal discharge process considerably
options.C: It ensures the nurse accurately understands vague patient statements
options.D: It legally protects the hospital from patient malpractice claims

explanation: Patients don't always use medical terms. Asking for clarification helps you clear up any confusion so you don't miss important symptoms! [learn more](GNS112_U3_T3#GNS112_U3_T3_h2)

question: During which phase of a patient interview does the nurse build initial trust and rapport?
explanation: Great job! The orientation phase is all about first impressions—introducing yourself, setting the tone, and helping the patient relax. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T3#GNS112_U3_T3_h3)

question: You want a patient to tell you all about their chest pain. Which question is best to ask?

options.A: Can you describe what your chest pain feels like?
options.B: You are not having difficulty breathing too, are you?
options.C: Is your chest pain sharp and stabbing right now?
options.D: Did this chest pain start after you ate heavy food?

explanation: Open-ended questions like this give patients room to talk freely and share details you might not get with a simple 'yes' or 'no' question. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T3#GNS112_U3_T3_h3)

question: What makes a therapeutic nurse-patient relationship special?

options.A: It is designed to last for a lifetime
options.B: It places equal focus on the personal needs of the nurse
options.C: It is strictly patient-centred and goal-oriented
options.D: It develops entirely without professional boundaries

explanation: Unlike friendships, professional nursing relationships are all about helping the patient reach their health goals. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T3#GNS112_U3_T3_h4)

question: Why do nurses need to maintain professional boundaries with patients?

options.A: They prevent the nurse from showing any empathy to patients
options.B: They stop patients from asking questions about their medications
options.C: They ensure that the nurse never has to talk about personal life
options.D: They maintain a safe and objective focus on patient care

explanation: Boundaries keep the care safe, clear, and focused entirely on the patient's healing journey. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T3#GNS112_U3_T3_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a psychological barrier to communication?

options.A: Depression following a chronic disease diagnosis
options.B: Loud machinery noise in the hospital corridor
options.C: High anxiety regarding a pending surgical procedure
options.D: Fear of an unknown medical diagnosis

explanation: You've got this! Loud noise is an environmental (physical) barrier, whereas worry, fear, and sadness happen inside the mind. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T3#GNS112_U3_T3_h5)

question: A patient with severe hearing loss is struggling to follow admission instructions. What should you do first?

options.A: Write all the instructions down and leave the room immediately
options.B: Ask a relative to make all decisions without consulting the patient
options.C: Face the patient directly and speak clearly without shouting
options.D: Raise your voice loudly so the patient can hear across the ward

explanation: Facing the patient lets them see your face and read your lips, making communication much easier without needing to shout. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T3#GNS112_U3_T3_h5)

question: What does the ethical principle of 'patient autonomy' mean in nursing?

options.A: The obligation to treat every patient with equal financial aid
options.B: The legal requirement to keep all clinical records locked away
options.C: The duty of the nurse to make all choices for the patient
options.D: The right of the patient to make their own health decisions

explanation: Autonomy is all about respect—giving patients the right to choose what happens to their own bodies and health. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T3#GNS112_U3_T3_h6)

question: When is it ethically okay for a nurse to break patient confidentiality?

options.A: When the nurse wants to discuss a case with friends off duty
options.B: Whenever the ward gets too busy to maintain patient records
options.C: Whenever a curious relative asks for the patient's lab results
options.D: When the patient poses an immediate danger to self or others

explanation: Safety always comes first! If a patient is about to harm themselves or someone else, keeping them safe overrides standard privacy rules. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T3#GNS112_U3_T3_h6)
